title: Introduction to Derivatives: The Mathematics of Change
subject: math

concepts.name: the_intuition_hook
concepts.instructions: Start by grounding the concept in reality. Explain that Calculus is the study of how things change. Use the analogy of a car's speedometer: a trip's average speed is easy (distance/time), but the speedometer shows your speed at this exact instant. Use 'show_image' to display a photo of a car speedometer or a rollercoaster drop. Use 'add_text' to define the Derivative as the 'instantaneous rate of change'. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: average_rate_gap
concepts.instructions: Explain that to find a slope, we usually need two points. This is the 'Average Rate of Change' (Slope of the Secant Line). Use 'show_image' to display a diagram of a Secant Line intersecting a curve at two points (since we cannot plot two lines at once). Use 'add_text' to show the formula \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}\) and explain that this calculates the slope between two distinct points. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: closing_the_gap
concepts.instructions: Explain the Limit: what happens if we move the two points closer and closer until they touch? The Secant becomes a Tangent. Use 'plot_function' to graph "x^2". Use 'add_text' to define the derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}\). Ask the student to look at the graph at x=1 and imagine a line skimming the edge of the curve at that exact spot. Call next_concept().

concepts.name: spotting_the_pattern
concepts.instructions: Instead of using the long limit formula every time, let's find a pattern. Use 'draw_table' with headers=["Function", "Derivative"] and rows=[["x^2", "2x"], ["x^3", "3x^2"], ["x^4", "4x^3"], ["x^10", "10x^9"]]. Use 'add_text' to ask the student: 'Look at the exponents. Can you guess the rule for x^n?' Call next_concept().

concepts.name: power_rule_algorithm
concepts.instructions: Confirm their guess: This is the Power Rule. You bring the power down and subtract one. Use 'draw_flowchart' with steps: ['Identify Exponent n', 'Multiply Coefficient by n', 'Subtract 1 from Exponent', 'Result is nx^{n-1}']. Use 'add_text' to show an example: \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^5) = 5x^4\). Call next_concept().

concepts.name: linear_behavior
concepts.instructions: Show how this works for straight lines. Use 'plot_function' to graph "2*x + 1". Use 'add_text' to explain: 'Notice this line never curves? Its slope is constant. Using the power rule on 2x^1 gives us 2x^0, which is just 2. The derivative of a linear term is just the coefficient.' Call next_concept().

concepts.name: visualizing_slopes
concepts.instructions: Synthesize the concepts visually. The derivative tells us if the function is rising or falling. Use 'plot_function' to graph "x^3 - 3*x". Use 'add_text' to guide them: 'Look at the graph. When the curve goes up, the derivative is positive. When it goes down, it is negative. Can you find the two spots (peaks/valleys) where the slope is exactly zero?' Call next_concept().

concepts.name: final_cheat_sheet
concepts.instructions: Wrap up with a summary table. Use 'add_text' to congratulate the student and emphasize these rules are the foundation of Calculus. Use 'draw_table' with headers=["Rule", "Formula"] and rows=[["Power Rule", "nx^{n-1}"], ["Constant", "0"], ["Linear", "c"], ["Sum Rule", "f'(x) + g'(x)"]]. Call finish_lesson().
